title: VeriHarm-Bench: Measuring Harmful Success in LLM Coding Agents Verifiably
abstract: arXiv:2611.03575v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large language model (LLM) coding agents increasingly operate with shell access, allowing them to write scripts, move files, alter permissions, and modify system configurations. However, an agent may achieve a user's goal while causing unintended harm, such as deleting unrelated files, weakening access controls, or corrupting data, in response to benign inputs without explicit jailbreaking. This failure mode is particularly important because apparent task success may reassure users that an agent behaved correctly, causing harmful side effects to go unnoticed. We call this harmful success: the agent successfully completes the intended benign task while simultaneously causing unintended harm. Despite its importance, harmful success is difficult to measure because conventional task-success metrics overlook harmful behaviors, while existing safety evaluations are often designed solely to assess harmful outcomes. translated_title: VeriHarm-Bench：可验证地测量LLM编程代理中的有害成功
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）编程代理越来越多地以shell访问权限运行，使其能够编写脚本、移动文件、更改权限和修改系统配置。然而，代理可能在实现用户目标的同时造成非预期的危害，例如删除无关文件、削弱访问控制或损坏数据，且这种情况可在响应良性输入时发生，而无需显式的越狱攻击。这种失败模式尤为重要，因为表面上的任务成功可能让用户确信代理行为正确，从而导致有害的副作用被忽视。我们将这种现象称为“有害成功”：代理在成功完成预期的良性任务的同时，造成了非预期的危害。尽管其重要性，有害成功难以测量，因为传统的任务成功指标忽略了有害行为，而现有的安全评估通常仅设计用于评估有害结果。我们提出了VeriHarm，一个自动……
tldr: 该论文提出了VeriHarm-Bench基准，首次定义并系统地测量LLM编程代理中的“有害成功”现象——即代理在成功完成良性任务的同时造成非预期的危害，而传统任务成功指标和现有安全评估均无法捕捉这一问题。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces VeriHarm-Bench, a benchmark that defines and verifiably measures "harmful success" in LLM coding agents—cases where agents complete benign tasks while simultaneously causing unintended harm, a failure mode overlooked by conventional success metrics and existing safety evaluations.
